slot.brief: Give XeF2, XeF4, XeF6 and ask which are square planar / which have lone pairs on the central atom — count lone pairs via VSEPR and match to shapes.

stem: Which of the following xenon compounds has the largest number of lone pairs on the central xenon atom?

verdicts.working: XeF₂ has 3 lone pairs on Xe; XeF₄ has 2; XeF₆ and XeO₃ each have 1. Thus XeF₂ has the most.

working:
Xe has 8 valence electrons.
XeF2: 2 bond pairs + 3 lone pairs = 5 pairs, so 3 lone pairs.
XeF4: 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs = 6 pairs, so 2 lone pairs.
XeF6: 6 bond pairs + 1 lone pair = 7 pairs, so 1 lone pair.
XeO3: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair = 4 pairs, so 1 lone pair.
Thus XeF2 has the maximum of 3 lone pairs.

Independent check: XeF₂ has 3 lone pairs on Xe; XeF₄ has 2; XeF₆ and XeO₃ each have 1. Thus XeF₂ has the most.
solution:
The number of lone pairs on Xe is determined from its valence shell and the bonding regions around it.
In XeF₂, Xe has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs; in XeF₄, XeF₆ and XeO₃, it has 2, 1 and 1 lone pairs, respectively.
Hence XeF₂ has the largest number of lone pairs: $3$.
